title: Data privacy at work
examples: What specific types of personal data should I be concerned about at work?
Can you give an example of when data minimisation is legally required?
How does data privacy affect my day-to-day job tasks?

explain.say: Today we are learning about data privacy in the workplace.

items: Personal data refers to information about an individual.
This includes names, addresses, and identification numbers.
It is any data that can identify a specific person.

explain.say: Understanding what counts as personal data is the first step.
Next we explore the principle of data minimisation.
Data minimisation means collecting only the data you truly need.
In a country like Canada, this principle is strongly emphasized in privacy laws.
For a real-life example, consider an HR system update.

items: Purpose | Data Collected | Is it Minimal?
Performance Review | Social Media Posts | No

faq.q: What is the difference between personal and confidential data?
faq.a: Personal data relates to an individual, while confidential data is information that is secret or private to an organization. They often overlap, but one can be sensitive without identifying a person.
asks: Is all private data personal data?
What is the difference between private and personal?

faq.q: If I need data for a project, can I collect everything just in case?
faq.a: No, that violates data minimisation. You must only collect the specific data points required to complete the stated project goal.
asks: Can I gather extra data just in case?
Is it okay to over-collect data?

faq.q: Does data privacy only apply when I am working on a computer?
faq.a: No, it applies to any form of data handling, whether it is written notes, verbal conversations, or digital files. The principle remains the same.
asks: Does this only apply to digital files?
Does data privacy cover spoken words?

faq.q: What if my manager asks for data that seems too much?
faq.a: You should politely question the necessity of the data using the principle of minimisation. Ask them to justify why every piece of information is needed.
asks: How do I question data requests?
What if my boss insists on the data?

faq.q: Does data minimisation mean I can delete data anytime?
faq.a: It means you should not keep data longer than it is necessary for the original, stated purpose. Retention policies guide when data must be deleted.
asks: How long must I keep data?
Can I delete data whenever I want?

facts: Personal data is any information relating to an identified or identifiable natural person.
Data minimisation requires collecting only the data strictly necessary for the specified purpose.
Data privacy laws aim to protect individuals from misuse of their personal information.
The principle requires that data should not be kept indefinitely once its purpose is fulfilled.

quiz.say: A company needs to process employee names and job titles for an internal directory. Which data points are essential?
quiz.why: These two pieces of information are directly and minimally required for creating a basic internal directory.

wrong.1: Salary and start date are usually not needed just to list names and job titles.
wrong.2: While useful, these are often too much data if only a directory listing is the goal.
wrong.3: The National ID number is highly sensitive and usually not required for a simple directory.

quiz.say: You are tasked with analyzing customer purchase trends. Which data collection approach follows data minimisation?
quiz.why: You only need the category of purchase, not the customer's full financial details, to analyze trends.

wrong.0: IP addresses can track location, which is often unnecessary when only the purchase category matters.
wrong.2: Full logs contain too much detail, including payment methods, which is excessive for trend analysis.
wrong.3: Names are personal data and are not necessary if you are only looking at general category trends.

quiz.say: If a project only requires knowing if a client is in Europe or Asia, which data collection is most appropriate?

options.show: Full Country Name and Zip Code
options.say: Full Country Name and Zip Code

quiz.why: Collecting only the continent region is the most minimal way to answer the geographical question.

wrong.1: This is too granular; the continent is sufficient for the stated need.
wrong.2: The email address is personal data and is not needed just to determine the continent.
wrong.3: Phone numbers are personal identifiers that go beyond the required geographical scope.
